pos.personaBrief: Wikipedia says his 4-4-2 at Grêmio and Palmeiras used quick transitions and counter-attacks, and Itatiaia stresses defensive strength. At Portugal he also played a passing style, so he is pragmatic more than possession-obsessed.

pro.personaBrief: Counter-attacking and aerial strength (headed goals at Grêmio, set pieces at Palmeiras) point to a vertical, direct side. Safe defensive midfielders Dinho and Goiano fit a low-risk build-up.

est.personaBrief: His sides held clear shapes (4-4-2, 4-2-2-2, back three) and he disliked changing the scheme (Record 2008), which suggests fixed roles. Paulo Nunes drifted behind Jardel, but the structure stayed defined.

lar.personaBrief: Arce's crosses, the wing-backs Cafu and Roberto Carlos in 2002, and Figo and Ronaldo on the wings in 2006 show he used the flanks a lot. Headed goals point to crosses as a main route.

blo.personaBrief: Wikipedia calls the 4-4-2 solid defensively and Itatiaia stresses defensive strength and discipline. Sources give little on pressing; Portugal's pressure in the Euro 2004 semi-final came only late, when chasing the game.

mar.personaBrief: No source names the marking system. Brazilian 'copeiro' sides with strong, committed defensive midfielders suggest firm duels and responsibility for opponents, with some use of zones.

pla.personaBrief: Record 2008 says he rarely changed the scheme for the opponent except when losing late. He kept his own plan and imposed choices, such as leaving Romario out and picking squad members by his own judgement.

res.personaBrief: Copeiro, pragmatic and trophy-driven: his sides won Libertadores finals on penalties and Euro 2004 reached the final through tactical preparation and pragmatism. Results come ahead of aesthetics.

sis.personaBrief: The 2002 squad worked as a collective ('familia Scolari') with duties for everyone, even Ronaldo, who did everything asked of him. He left out Romario and Djalminha, so no star was above the group.

jog.personaBrief: Aerial play, fouls and fighting spirit at Grêmio in 1996, strong volantes and a 'copeiro' style. The squads were physical and combative, though Portugal 2004 also had technical players.

bas.personaBrief: He mixed experienced players with young talent, as at Grêmio 1995, and called up Kaka and Kleberson in 2002. Titles still rested on established players like Figo, Rui Costa and the Brazilian veterans.

lid.personaBrief: Arce describes firmness with affection and no aggression, a family group where he gave everything for the players. He was still the boss: he vetoed Baía and said 'nobody will change my mind' on squad selection.
